summary: Both of my v13 findings are substantively repaired and I re-derived each independently rather than trusting the claim. The frozen Claude v11 verdict is now bound at 405bade0... with its verdict and finding ids recorded accurately, closing the missing-lane gap; all eighteen pins reproduce, up from fifteen. The DCIC-V7-A1 date is corrected to v10 in both places, and I re-measured v9 and v10 myself to confirm it - v9 carries no codexv7.advisories key at all, v10 is where it first appears. The two historical honesty blocks were opened deliberately, declared on the roster, and edited in withdraw-and-restate form ('at v10 (not v9)') rather than silently rewritten, which preserves the record that they were once wrong. The roster is exact, every substantive key is byte-identical to v13, and the remeasurement is exact on all three files at live HEAD, so the dispatch's drift allowance was again unnecessary. One defect remains, and it is one this successor introduced: having added claude2v11 to the ledger, v14 gives CLAUDE-V11-ADV-1 no folded/not-folded disposition. I enumerated all twenty recorded advisories and tested each; nineteen are disposed and this is the only one that is not - and I discarded a false positive on DCIC-V4-A2 before filing, since the 'DCIC-V4-A1/A2' shorthand does dispose it. The advisory is in fact already folded by v14's own date correction, so this is a one-line credit rather than new work - the same half-folded shape that CLAUDE-V11-S1 once described for CLAUDE-V6-ADV-1.
